decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its target interest rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed officially started raising interest rates after holding them at 1 percent previously.

changes.quote: Although incoming inflation data are somewhat elevated, a portion of the increase in recent months appears to have been due to transitory factors.
changes.explanation: The Committee notes that higher recent inflation has some temporary causes.

changes.quote: The Committee perceives the upside and downside risks to the attainment of both sustainable growth and price stability for the next few quarters are roughly equal.
changes.explanation: The Fed now explicitly includes price stability alongside sustainable growth when balancing risks.

changes.quote: With underlying inflation still expected to be relatively low, the Committee believes that policy accommodation can be removed at a pace that is likely to be measured.
changes.explanation: The Fed signals that future rate increases will likely happen at a steady, measured pace.

changes.quote: Nonetheless, the Committee will respond to changes in economic prospects as needed to fulfill its obligation to maintain price stability.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this language to emphasize its readiness to adjust policy if economic conditions change.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee believes that, even after this action, the stance of monetary policy remains accommodative and, coupled with robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing ongoing support to economic activity.
With underlying inflation still expected to be relatively low, the Committee believes that policy accommodation can be removed at a pace that is likely to be measured.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.67% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.62% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.32% would fall by about $15.63 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 5.6%, and employers added an average of 292k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.9% over the past year (May 2004); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -13 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve plans to continue removing monetary policy accommodation at a measured pace. The educational forecast suggests future actions will depend on incoming data regarding inflation and economic growth.
